newsitem.title: JAPAN: Philips, Sony, Pioneer start licensing DVD patents.
newsitem.headline: Philips, Sony, Pioneer start licensing DVD patents.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday that it, Sony Corp and Pioneer Electronic Corp had started licensing their patents on manufacturing technology for digital video discs (DVD).
Philips said in a statement that Sony and Pioneer had authorised Philips to operate the licensing programme.
The licences will be available for a royalty of 3.5 percent for DVD players and five U.S. cents per disc, the statement said.
The three companies are members of a 10-firm DVD consortium under which the world's major electronics companies jointly developed DVD technology.

But at present, because the patents held by the three companies cover only part of the technology needed to make DVDs and DVD products, obtaining a patent from Philips would not be sufficient to allow a company to begin making the products.
The consortium members are at odds with each other over how to divide the royalties and licensing fees.
A Sony spokesman said the three companies will continue to negotiate with other consortium members on providing one-stop licensing of the patents.
A spokesman for Toshiba Corp, a member of the consortium, declined to comment on the three firms' move, but said negotiations among the 10 firms were still going on.
